messages:
sam: FYI customer reported JSON mode streaming coming back with a truncated object mid-brace. they get a parse error downstream and our SDK raises \"InvalidStructuredOutput\". stack: mobile app -> customer proxy -> our edge -> upstream. request_id=rdw-8a7c

support-bot: Thanks, ticket linked: https://support.redwood.ai/t/4201. Escalating to infra/eng. :rotating_light:

maria: Can you paste the raw last few bytes the client received? even a redacted snippet helps (plus the request_id). Also capture the connection close reason from the edge logs if available.

sam: request_id rdw-8a7c. here's the final bytes from the client's TCP stream (redacted):

```
..."choices":[{"delta":{"content":{"json":{"id":"1234","state":"com"
```

The stream ends right there, no closing braces. Client tries to parse and fails. Error on client: `JSONDecodeError: Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes`

ingrid: Uploading the edge logs now — I see the connection FIN immediately after a keepalive probe from the client. Upstream shows TLS close with `errno=104` (connection reset by peer) around the same timestamp. This smells like an intermediate proxy or the customer's client tearing the connection while our runtime was still sending the final bytes.

ben: Two quick paths: 1) short-term, advise customer to buffer until final `data: [DONE]` or implement minimal reassembly+retry for truncated JSON. 2) long-term, make our streaming SSE include an explicit final framing token that is robust to chunk boundary truncation (e.g., `X-Stream-Finish: <id>` or `data: __REDWOOD_FIN__`).

maria: For troubleshooting: can you run a repro that simulates an abrupt client close? simple curl command to mimic SSE + immediate close:

```
# simulate consumer that closes early after N bytes
curl --no-buffer "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?mode=json" -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" --output - | dd bs=1 count=150
```

That reproduces a similar mid-object cutoff in my local test. If you can produce the exact count where the customer's client cuts, we can reproduce deterministically.

sam: I ran that with count=142 and reproduced. logs attached in ticket. Customer is on a corporate proxy (BlueProxy 2.1) that has a 2s idle timeout and sometimes sends a FIN if it suspects a stalled stream.

ingrid: Action items from infra perspective:
- increase `proxy_buffer_size` and `proxy_read_timeout` for the edge LB to tolerate longer keepalives. snippet:
```
proxy_buffer_size 16k;
proxy_read_timeout 10s;
proxy_send_timeout 10s;
```
- add extra heartbeat SSE `:h` comment every 3s when streaming structured JSON to keep corporate proxies from thinking the stream is idle.

maria: I'll add a temporary server-side finalizer that emits `data: __RDW_STREAM_END__\n\n` right before connection close so clients that stop early can still detect a truncated finalization. We'll roll behind a feature flag for 24h and monitor errors.

ben: Also flagging SDK team: should add a best-effort streaming parser that tolerates single-brace truncation and requests a resume when possible (idempotent tokens). cc @deploy-bot for a canary push.

deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled for the feature-flagged finalizer to 5% of traffic at 00:30 UTC.

sam: Customer notified with workaround (buffer and retry) and ETA for the short-term server finalizer. will follow up after canary. :thumbsup:

maria: Added unit/regression tests to catch truncated-chunk parse path. will also add an integration test that closes the client midstream to ensure we don't regress.

ingrid: I'm going to open an observability alert to track `structured_streams.truncated_count` and a diagnostic histogram for `last_chunk_size` so we can detect repeat offenders (specific customers/proxies).

sam: thanks all. I'll update the support ticket when the canary is green and include the customer's proxy logs.

ben: one more note — recommend customer try using a small exponential backoff + resume token approach in their proxy to avoid hard FINs during transient network reshapes.

support-bot: Ticket rdw-8a7c updated: short-term mitigation suggested, canary scheduled. :white_check_mark:
